title: Bonuses reported for officers and key employees of City-paid organizations
question: Which officers, key employees and highest-paid staff of organizations the City pays were reported as receiving bonus or incentive pay, and how much?
finding: 1,405 returns from 352 City-paid organizations for tax years ending 2020 to 2026 carry a compensation schedule, and they report 2,484 bonus or incentive payments at 135 organizations, $538.1 million in all. 81% of the money is at Dignity Health Dba St Mary's Medical Ctr ($285.0 million), Delta Dental Plan of California ($113.3 million) and California Pacific Medical Center ($37.8 million), where City payments were never more than 0.05% of revenue in any year on file: 1,425 of the payments are at organizations where the City supplied under 1% of revenue that year. The largest single figure is $17.0 million (Lloyd H Dean, Chief Executive Officer, Dignity Health Dba St Mary's Medical Ctr, year ended 30 June 2022). The next table keeps only organizations for which the City is a main funder.
how: From the compensation schedule (Schedule J, Part II) of every Form 990 on file for the organizations the City paid most: column B(ii), bonus and incentive compensation, from the filing organization and from related organizations, for each listed officer, director, key employee and highest-paid employee. A person listed by two related filers with the same figures is counted once. Names and titles are as the returns print them. City money is the Controller’s record of payments to the organization, spread onto its tax year by days of overlap; the share is of the revenue on the same return and is capped at 150%. Largest first. Where the organization’s tax number was matched by hand and has not been verified, the last column says so.
limits: For a bonus, the question is whether the board approves it; 339 of the 401 returns that report one also say that a compensation committee or the board approved the top officer’s pay. Size alone says nothing: the largest are at very large organizations that the City pays for particular services and does not fund in any general sense. The compensation schedule (Schedule J) follows from the return’s question whether any listed person was paid more than $150,000, so bonuses to people below that line, and at organizations where nobody reaches it, are not on any return. The bonus column is defined by the tax form as bonus and incentive pay; organizations differ in what they put there, and some record a retention payment, a signing payment or a payout under a long-term plan in it. Pay on this schedule is for the calendar year ending inside the tax year, so it does not line up exactly with City fiscal years.
